title: Communication-Constrained Estimation of Federated Cross Means under Sparse Overlap
banked_reason: Graded tier 'incremental' against target 'field': the advertised sharp positive-budget frontier remains open, while the proved communication-specific result is only a zero-message indistinguishability lower bound.
gap_reasons: The advertised sharp one-round communication frontier is not delivered: every positive-budget case and the unequal-site extension remain open, while the proved communication-specific result is only a zero-message indistinguishability lower bound.
The note also calls the zero-budget elbow ‘settled,’ but proves only R⋆comp ≥ 1/4, without a matching upper bound establishing the risk or frontier there.
The centralized result is a wide bracket with a logarithmic gap in its dimension-dependent term.
proof_attempt_summary: The run repaired the fixed-site experiment, audited generic distribution-recovery collisions, transferred a centralized iid-submodel lower bracket, and proved a two-point 1/4 lower bound whenever either site has zero communication budget. The reciprocal-polynomial identity did not become a finite-bit, coefficient-controlled positive-budget estimator, and no matching sampled- transcript converse was obtained; those two missing constructions are the advertised kernel.
tldr: For the fixed-site finite-cell specialization, the proved contribution is a structural and boundary result, not a matched communication frontier. The complementary class is nonempty under the exact allocation-adjusted mass-ratio condition and retains arbitrarily sparse positive cells. The note records exact message counts and risk bounds for several comparator procedures and proves a bracket for the centralized product experiment. A new exact elbow shows that \(R^{\star}_{\mathrm{comp}}\geq1/4\) whenever \(\min\{B_1,B_2\}=0\). The reciprocal-weighted frontier for \(B_1,B_2\geq1\), a coefficient-controlled protocol, fixed-size de-Poissonization, a same-transcript converse, and any unequal-\(K\) extension remain open.
gap: Existing causal work identifies the pooled ATE and supplies oracle or asymptotic estimators. Acharya et al. and Yuan--Guo--Huang solve strong common-law recovery or nonparametric estimation baselines, and fixed-kernel protocols solve another substantial portion, but none presently gives a matched simultaneous sampled frontier for heterogeneous reciprocal-weighted cross means on sparse finite cells.
fill: Optimize and fully compare the exact-subhistogram, full-sample type-grid, Acharya and Yuan--Guo--Huang virtual-terminal recovery, and known-kernel envelopes; then either prove a strictly sharper finite-alphabet reciprocal-lifting protocol with a same-experiment transcript converse, or drop the causal-specific frontier and report the optimized generic instantiation. Extend to unequal \(K\)-site budgets only in the former case.
